newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BCE wheat futures drop, maize ends mixed.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BCE wheat futures drop, maize ends mixed.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices dropped for all maturities in the Budapest Commodities Exchange's (BCE) grain section on Thursday and traders expect the downward trend to continue.
"Prices are still too high, further drops are very likely," said Mihaly Otvos of OTP Forex.
Milling wheat prices fell by 100 to 400 forints, with benchmark 1997 August ending at 22,000 forints, down 100.
"There are many speculative deals around the 22,000 forint level as everybody is still guessing export prices," Otvos added.
Maize futures ended 40 to 150 forints higher for the nearest and most distant maturities -- December 1996, November and December 1997 -- and fell 90 to 150 forints for all other 1997 maturities.
"There are only three days of trade remaining until the December maturity and those who do not want to deliver try to get out of their contracts," Otvos said.
Total turnover on the BCE grain section was 887 contracts or 426.5 million forints, below Wednesday's 527.6 million forints turnover. Maize and wheat accounted for 711 lots.
"Turnover has been getting lower during the last weeks as dealers are waiting for information to trade on before opening new positions," Otvos said.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
